definition: VEX Robotics is a robotics program for elementary through university students, and a subset of Innovation First International.
details: The VEX Robotics competitions and programs were overseen by the Robotics Education & Competition Foundation (RECF) until May 2026, when VEX split from the foundation and created the Global Robotics & Science Foundation (GRSF) to oversee competition. VEX Robotics Competition was named the largest robotics competition in the world by Guinness World Records. There are four leagues of VEX Robotics competitions designed for different age groups and skill levels. The VEX V5 Robotics Competition (V5RC), the largest, is targeted toward middle and high school students. The VEX IQ Robotics Competition (VIQRC) is targeted toward elementary and middle school students. The VEX AI Robotics Competition is a 'spinoff' for high school and college-level students. The competition features no driver control periods, hence the name 'VEX AI'. VEX U is a robotics competition for university students. The game is similar to V5RC, but traditionally features a unique ruleset with more relaxed rules on the construction of their robots, and teams consisting of two robots. explainer.lead: VEX Robotics is a student robotics program spanning elementary through university levels and is a subset of Innovation First International. Its competition was named the largest robotics competition in the world by Guinness World Records.

tiers.eli5: It's like a sports league where kids build and program robots, with different divisions for different ages and skill levels.
tiers.practitioner: Teams design and program robots for the four age-tiered leagues, with the VEX V5 Robotics Competition aimed at older students. The governing structure is a pitfall to track: the RECF oversaw competitions until May 2026, when VEX split off and created the Global Robotics & Science Foundation (GRSF).
tiers.paperLevel: A program organized into four leagues by age group and skill level; competition oversight moved from the RECF to the newly created GRSF in May 2026. It is an educational and competitive program, not a formal algorithmic method.
